request.questionText: In 1990, the United Nations created a single measure that ranges between zero and one -- the Human Development Index (HDI) -- to summarize health, education, and economic status for world countries. Below is the equation for a fitted model to predict response variable HDI in terms of two predictor variables: Life expectancy and average years of School. HDI = -0.34 + (0.01 * Life) + (0.02 * School) + E Which of the following is an accurate interpretation of the coefficient for years of School? Select all correct answers.

choices.label: A
choices.text: When the average years of School in a country increases by one year, we expect HDI to increase by 0.02, irrespective of variation in Life expectancy.

choices.label: B
choices.text: We expect HDI to increase by 0.02 for every one-year increase in the School variable, after adjusting for the simultaneous effect of Life expectancy on HDI.

choices.label: C
choices.text: When comparing countries with similar life expectancies but a difference of one year in years of School, we'd expect their HDIs to differ by 0.02.

choices.label: D
choices.text: An estimated slope for the overall relationship between years of School and HDI.
